faq.a: Mandana is associated with the Persian form مَنْدَانَا, whose core sense is mandana; a persian legendary queen.

faq.q: What is the origin of Mandana?
faq.a: Mandana is associated with Persian. Mandana is Persian ماندانا (Māndānā), the name of a legendary queen, mother of Cyrus. It is used as a female given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Mandana can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Mandana should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Māndānā is a Persian name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Mandana mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Mandana is rendered ماندانا and carries the sense ماندانا، فارسی ملکہ.

faq.q: What does Mandana mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Mandana is rendered ماندانا and carries the sense ماندانا، ملکه افسانه‌ای.
A romanized syllable approximation is man-da-na. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Mandana?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Mandana, mandana. Script forms are ماندانا, مَنْدَانَا, मंदाना.

faq.q: Is Mandana a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
